instruction: Check the 2023 book reading data spreadsheet located on your desktop, find the book with the fastest reading speed in words per day, and enter its title into the 'book_list_result.docx' file on your desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding the book with the highest reading speed (words per day) from the spreadsheet. Verified with Python: 'The Shining' has 24767.17 words/day (Row 11), which is the maximum. The evaluator checks if the DOCX file contains this book title.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts text content from DOCX file using python-docx library with proper error handling
Metric correctly checks if extracted text contains expected book title with case-insensitive matching and whitespace normalization
Expected value 'The Shining' is verified in metadata as the book with highest reading speed (24767.17 words/day)
Postconfig properly saves the DOCX file before verification using Ctrl+S
Complete coverage: evaluator verifies the core requirement (book title present in DOCX)

Metric parameter handling is CORRECT: when expected.type='rule', metric receives rules dict directly {'text': 'The Shining'} and accesses it with expected.get('text') - the static warning is a false positive
